subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, and should heartbeat expose matching config fields or keep its current implicit stable phase behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining fix defines new public scheduling semantics and config/API surface that affect persisted jobs and existing operator expectations.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit, backward-compatible `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current anchored fixed-interval semantics and rely on heartbeat stable phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime cadence controls
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron, with observability and migration requirements called out up front.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit, backward-compatible `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the cron stagger surface and public scheduling contract that this decision would extend.
